module_summary: OSDHistory.h/.cpp write the Sony OSD play-history record (mc?:/<region>DATA-SYSTEM/history) on launch, ported from upstream OPL; system.cpp:1343-1378 is the only caller. bgm.cpp is the theme background-music player: an Ogg/Vorbis decode thread and an audsrv feeder thread around a 768 KB static ring, with a reopening read layer for SD2PSX descriptor loss and an on-the-fly Ogg serial/CRC fix; its state lives in a single-instance BgmPlayer class (include/bgmplayer.h) behind the C-style bgm* API of sound.h. cheatman.cpp (PS2rd-derived) parses .cht text into a lazily allocated ~1 MB cheat table, flattens it for ee_core, and packs the in-game-menu cheats page; cheatconfig.cpp stores Select-mode picks by name in the game CFG. config.h is the config API: file/key name macros for every setting plus thin NULL-guarded inline wrappers over ConfigSet.

reusable_helpers.name: read_text_file
reusable_helpers.what: reads a whole file into a malloc'd NUL-terminated buffer (open/lseek/read)

reusable_helpers.name: trim_str
reusable_helpers.what: trims leading and trailing white space in place

reusable_helpers.name: is_empty_str
reusable_helpers.what: 1 when a string holds only white space

reusable_helpers.name: chr_idx
reusable_helpers.what: index of a character in a string or -1 (strchr equivalent)

reusable_helpers.name: cheatConfigNormalize
reusable_helpers.what: lower-cases a string and collapses/trims white space for name comparison

reusable_helpers.name: oggCrcDelta
reusable_helpers.what: Ogg CRC-32 (poly 0x04C11DB7) table build and CRC delta for a flipped header bit

reusable_helpers.name: bgmSourceReopen
reusable_helpers.what: reopens a FILE* by path and seeks back to the saved position, with bounded retries

reusable_helpers.name: osdHistorySetDate
reusable_helpers.what: packs year/month/day into the 16-bit OSD datestamp

findings.title: BgmPlayer: single-instance class reached only through two thread trampolines and five one-line forwarding wrappers
findings.problem: BgmPlayer has exactly one instance, the file-static gBgm (bgm.cpp:56), and no code outside bgm.cpp names the class (include/bgmplayer.h is included only by bgm.cpp:14). Every outside use goes through the C-style sound.h functions, which only forward (bgm.cpp:905-928), and the thread bodies need two static trampolines (bgm.cpp:58-66) because they are member functions. The ring buffer and the running flags already had to stay file-static outside the class (bgm.cpp:72-73).
findings.fix: Make the BgmPlayer members file-static variables in bgm.cpp and the member functions static functions, name the public ones directly bgmStart/bgmStop/bgmQuiesce/isBgmPlaying/bgmDiscretionaryIoAllowed, pass the thread functions to CreateThread directly, and delete include/bgmplayer.h.
findings.benefit: ~55 lines removed (50-line header replaced by ~15 static declarations, 9 trampoline lines, ~20 forwarding lines). No ELF change expected beyond a few bytes of call indirection (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: grep BgmPlayer|bgmplayer.h over the repo: code hits only in include/bgmplayer.h and src/core/bgm.cpp; other hits are docs/CPP-CONVERSION-PLAN.md:388-396 (the conversion that introduced it) and .github/scripts/test_audio_threads.py / test_bgm_source.py, which locate functions by the text 'BgmPlayer::waitForRoom(' etc. and would need their anchors updated. Callers of the sound.h API: sound.cpp:50, textures.cpp:933 (gBgmInRead). Confidence Med because the class form follows the repo's own C++ conversion plan.

findings.title: OSDHistory: unused date getters, no-op DEBUG_PRINTF calls, commented-out loop and three stray includes of OSDHistory.h
findings.problem: osdHistoryGetYear/Month/Date have no use anywhere. DEBUG_PRINTF is defined empty at :33 and never redefined, so its 8 calls compile to nothing. :217-223 is a commented-out loop from the original. The three switch arms at :45-58 all set the same size. sysvmc.cpp, sysneutrino.cpp and sysdisc.cpp include OSDHistory.h but use nothing from it (only system.cpp:1350,1378 calls AddHistoryRecordUsingFullPath).
findings.fix: Delete the three getters, the DEBUG_PRINTF define and its calls, and the commented-out loop; set size once after the switch (or pick only the icon pointer in it); drop the OSDHistory.h include from sysvmc.cpp, sysneutrino.cpp and sysdisc.cpp.
findings.benefit: ~25 lines removed; no ELF change (constexpr getters and empty macros generate no code) (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: grep osdHistoryGet(Year|Month|Date) whole repo: only OSDHistory.h:83-85 and a docs mention. grep DEBUG_PRINTF in src/: only OSDHistory.cpp:33 (define) and its 8 calls; other hits are in .github/scripts tests and IOP modules with their own defines. grep MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES|HistoryEntry|osdHistorySetDate in src/: only OSDHistory.cpp. grep AddHistoryRecord in src/: system.cpp:1350,1378 only. sysvmc.cpp:41, sysneutrino.cpp:42, sysdisc.cpp:43 are bare includes.

findings.title: OSDHistory.h carries a 79-line block of disassembly notes from the original OSDSYS
findings.problem: Lines 3-73 are reverse-engineering notes (hex dumps of record bytes and a pseudo-C transcription of OSDSYS 1.00 code at fixed addresses) that the ported implementation in OSDHistory.cpp:126-264 already embodies; only the 'Conclusion' field layout at :74-80 documents the struct below it. The block is upstream-derived (INFERRED: same notes as upstream OPL).
findings.fix: Keep the 6-line field layout (:74-80) next to struct HistoryEntry and delete the rest of the comment.
findings.benefit: ~72 comment lines removed; no binary effect.
findings.evidence: Read OSDHistory.h:1-101 and OSDHistory.cpp:1-298; the logic of :28-72 is the loop at OSDHistory.cpp:173-260. Upstream origin of the comment not checked (no upstream checkout in scope): INFERRED.

findings.title: cheatman parser: parse_line wrapper re-tests is_cheat_code, make_code has a redundant zero branch, term_str callback has one caller
findings.problem: parse_buf already calls is_cheat_code (:346) and enters the parser branch for code lines and empty lines; parse_line (:187-200) runs is_cheat_code again only to return a zero code for the empty-line case, plus a per-line LOG. make_code pre-zeroes address/value and then has a failure branch that zeroes again (:149-153). term_str (:227-240) is a generic callback walker with a NULL check whose only caller passes is_cmt_str, which re-runs strlen at every character.
findings.fix: In parse_buf, call make_code directly when is_cheat_code(line) is true and skip the line otherwise; delete parse_line. Assign code.addr/val from the sscanf results unconditionally (they stay 0 on a short parse). Replace term_str+is_cmt_str with one inline scan that cuts the line at the first '#' or '//'.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed; a few hundred bytes of .text at most (INFERRED; static functions, likely inlined already).
findings.evidence: All five functions are static in cheatman.cpp; grep term_str|is_cmt_str|parse_line|make_code in src: only cheatman.cpp. term_str called only at :342; parse_line only at :354. is_cheat_code returns 0 for an empty string (i==0 != CODE_DIGITS), so the zero code from parse_line for non-code lines is the only thing it adds. Note: the per-line LOG at :193 goes away with parse_line.

findings.title: load_cheats: read_text_file's maxsize option is never used and the parse tail duplicates load_cheats_buf
findings.problem: read_text_file's only caller passes maxsize 0 (:476), so the size-limit branch (:411-415) is dead. load_cheats (:467-489) repeats load_cheats_buf's ensureCheatTable/parse_buf/mode-return sequence (:495-507).
findings.fix: Drop the maxsize parameter and its branch; make load_cheats read the file, call load_cheats_buf(buf), free the buffer and return that result.
findings.benefit: ~12 lines removed; no measurable ELF change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: grep read_text_file in src: cheatman.cpp:388,393,476 only. load_cheats called at supportbase.cpp:1811, load_cheats_buf at supportbase.cpp:1779; both return values are used the same way (>=0 then sbCheatsSelect). Order change (table allocated after the read instead of before) does not change results: a failed read returns -1 either way.

findings.title: parse_buf computes each cheat's Select-mode default that cheatConfigLoadSelections always recomputes
findings.problem: parse_buf sets enabled = (gCheatMode == 0) || cheatConfigIsMasterCode(name) for every cheat. In Select mode (load returns 1) both load paths call sbCheatsSelect (supportbase.cpp:1785,1840), whose cheatConfigLoadSelections first resets every entry to cheatConfigIsMasterCode(name) (cheatconfig.cpp:72-73). The parser's master-code test is therefore overwritten every time, and it is the only reason cheatman.cpp includes cheatconfig.h.
findings.fix: Set enabled = 1 in parse_buf (Auto mode runs every cheat; Select mode is reset by cheatConfigLoadSelections) and drop the cheatconfig.h include from cheatman.cpp.
findings.benefit: ~3 lines and one header dependency removed; saves one name normalisation (2 x 129-byte buffers) per parsed cheat (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read supportbase.cpp:1730-1840: sbCheatsSelect(cheatMode,...) calls cheatConfigLoadSelections when cheatMode==1, after both load_cheats_buf (:1779-1785) and load_cheats (:1811, :1840). load_cheats/load_cheats_buf have no other callers. grep cheatConfig in cheatman.cpp: only :27 (include) and :369. Med: relies on every future Select-mode path going through sbCheatsSelect.

findings.title: cheatman.h: CHEAT_VERSION, CR and SPACE are never used
findings.problem: No C/C++ source uses CHEAT_VERSION, CR or SPACE from this header; NUL and LF (:46-47) are the only character constants the cheat code uses. CHEAT_VERSION's only other mention is a text anchor in .github/scripts/test_cheat_capacity.py:24.
findings.fix: Delete the three definitions and move the test's slice anchor to the next line (for example 'constexpr int MAX_HOOKS').
findings.evidence: grep CHEAT_VERSION|\bCR\b|\bSPACE\b over *.c,*.cpp,*.h,*.py,*.yaml: definitions at cheatman.h:37,48-49; test_cheat_capacity.py:24 (index anchor); test_neutrino_cheats.py:49 defines its own SPACE; other CR/SPACE hits are comments or unrelated locals in IOP modules (smb.c:830, smbman-ra smb.c:1207) that do not include cheatman.h.

findings.title: Dead setting key CONFIG_OPL_ENABLE_ANALOG_NAV and its dialog id UICFG_ENABLE_ANALOG_NAV
findings.problem: The Left Stick Navigation option was removed (dialogs.cpp:2263-2268 says it is never coming back), but its config key and its UI id remain. Neither name, nor the key string enable_analog_nav, is used anywhere else.
findings.evidence: grep ENABLE_ANALOG_NAV|enable_analog_nav|AnalogNav whole repo: config.h:114, dialogs.h:27 and the comment at dialogs.cpp:2266 only. Removing the enum member renumbers the later UICFG_* ids; grep shows they are used only symbolically in dialogs tables (INFERRED from the UI_ITEMS enum being a plain id list).

findings.title: config.h comments point to files that no longer exist (src/libview.c, opl.c, src/config.c)
findings.problem: The comments name libViewStoreToConfig in src/libview.c, readConfigPathRedirect() in opl.c and src/config.c; the code now lives in src/ui/libview.cpp:351, src/app/settingsio.cpp:296 and src/core/config.cpp, and none of the named .c files exists.
findings.evidence: Glob src/{config,opl,libview}.c: no files. grep readConfigPathRedirect|libViewStoreToConfig in src: settingsio.cpp:296, libview.cpp:351.

findings.title: bgm.cpp: stale section banner, orphaned member comment and two unused includes
findings.problem: The 'Theme Sound Effects' banner (:21-22) heads nothing: sound effects moved to sfx.cpp. :116-120 describes bytesPerMs_ and roomTarget_, which now live in include/bgmplayer.h:46-47, and sits above an unrelated function. Nothing in bgm.cpp calls a pad.h function, and the only timer-like call, SetAlarm, is a kernel.h syscall that opl.h:5 already brings in (INFERRED for timer.h).
findings.fix: Delete the banner, move or delete the orphaned comment, and drop the timer.h and pad.h includes.
findings.evidence: Read bgm.cpp:1-928 and include/bgmplayer.h; compared against include/pad.h prototypes (startPads, readPads, getKey, padRumble...): none appears in bgm.cpp. timer.h contents not read (SDK header), so the timer.h part is INFERRED.
